note: Phase A.1/1.3 asks for min/max/median of each NPDD parameter across INDEPENDENTLY-fit literature sources, to justify (or correct) S2's +/-50% perturbation range. Gate A found and fixed a real citation-scoping bug (Bayfol's dn_max had been cited from a different experiment in the source paper than the one being fit -- see docs/parameter_provenance.md) and switched the fit's second free parameter from D0 to dn_max, which dropped NRMSE on the two in-regime Bayfol HX series from 0.73-0.87 to 0.17-0.29 (GOOD, best of 10 random-start fits -- see results_literature_fit.json). This is real progress, but it does not unblock a spread claim: both good fits come from the SAME paper, SAME K, SAME material -- two exposure-intensity series of one figure, not independent sources. A parameter 'spread' computed from two non-independent series of one medium is not what S2's range justification needs, and would overstate confidence the same way the original 3-poor-fits version of this file warned against, just from the other direction (too few real degrees of freedom, not too poor a fit). The PQ/PMMA fit (also 'GOOD' by NRMSE) is explicitly excluded: it's out-of-range (K=24.94 vs the paper's tested 1.96-15.71 rad/um) and dn_max is not identifiable from a still-rising, unsaturated curve regardless of NRMSE (docs/parameter_provenance.md) -- its low NRMSE reflects an under-constrained fit, not a usable parameter estimate.

excluded_out_of_range_or_underconstraine.reason: K outside tested grid; curve never saturates, so dn_max is not identifiable regardless of NRMSE

residual_flag: The two in-regime Bayfol dn_max_fit values (0.1356 vs 0.05017) disagree by 2.7x despite describing the same material at two exposure intensities -- a single shared saturation ceiling should not vary this much between series of one figure. Reported directly in Section 6, not smoothed over. Suggests real remaining fit degeneracy even within the 'GOOD' NRMSE band.
what_would_resolve_this: A real independent-source spread claim needs at least one more genuinely independent medium confirmed in-regime, which needs either: (a) access to the two paywalled Optica NPDD papers (Kelly & Sheridan 2011, Gleeson et al. 2008), which report exactly the multi-K growth-curve families this model was designed against and would be a real second data point, not a second series of the same figure, or (b) resolving the 2.7x dn_max disagreement between the two existing Bayfol series (e.g. a joint fit sharing one dn_max across both, checking whether that's still achievable at reasonable NRMSE) before treating even this one medium as internally consistent enough to anchor a spread.
